failure_summary.description: State abbreviations were passed as cities, or a neighborhood was passed as the hotel city instead of using the city and neighborhood fields.
Agents skipped an unsatisfied update or repeated searches and filters for domains or constraints already handled.
Initial search results were left unsaved or duplicated in extra bare calls.
Agents added avoidable date conversions or extra flight date constraints not requested by the user.

patch.reasoning: Most cache, persistence, and date-handling problems are already explicitly covered by the skill, so repeating those rules would not fill a gap. The recurring field-mapping errors warrant clearer location examples, and the hotel star request exposes that the exact-value rule currently names ratings but not star counts.

edits.target: Map cities to `city`, states or regions to `state`, neighborhoods to `neighborhood` while retaining the full provided name, and airport codes to the corresponding airport-code field; do not put a state abbreviation in `city` or truncate a location value.
edits.content: Map cities to `city`, states or regions to `state`, neighborhoods to `neighborhood` while retaining the full provided name, and airport codes to the corresponding airport-code field; do not put a state abbreviation in `city` or truncate a location value. A two-letter U.S. state abbreviation supplied as a location belongs in `state`, with `city` unset unless a city was also provided. For a city plus neighborhood, keep them separate (for example, `city="Atlanta"` and `neighborhood=["Midtown Atlanta"]`), rather than using the neighborhood as the city.

edits.target: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.
edits.content: For numeric ratings and hotel star counts, treat a single numeric value without range, minimum, or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.
